articles.title: A-222E Bereg-E: Vũ khí "độc nhất vô nhị" của Nga có thể xóa sổ cánh quân đổ bộ đối phương
articles.text:
Tổ hợp pháo bờ biển di động A-222 Bereg do Nga chế tạo được cho là độc nhất vô nhị, không có loại nào tương tự trên thế giới, sở hữu nhiều ưu điểm vượt trội.
Tổ hợp pháo bờ biển di động A-222 Bereg do Nga chế tạo hiện được biên chế số lượng lớn trong Lực lượng phòng thủ bờ biển của nước này.
A-222 Bereg được cho là độc nhất vô nhị.
Chúng có thể tác chiến độc lập hoặc phối hợp với các tổ hợp tên lửa 4K44 Redut, K-300P Bation-P, Bal-E hay 4K51 Rubezh, hình thành một mạng lưới hỏa lực phòng thủ bờ biển liên hoàn, nhiều tầng, nhiều lớp.
A-222 Bereg được cho là độc nhất vô nhị, không có loại nào tương tự trên thế giới, sở hữu nhiều ưu điểm vượt trội:
Thứ nhất, cơ động nhanh. A-222 Bereg có khả năng thần tốc vượt qua các địa hình phức tạp nhờ được đặt trên khung gầm xe việt dã bánh lốp với 4 cầu chủ động của xe MAZ-543, để đến vị trí triển khai trận địa chiến đấu, kịp thời khai hỏa tiêu diệt và chế áp lực lượng chiến đấu mặt biển hay ven biển của địch.
Pháo A-222 Bereg có thể bắn trúng các tàu cao tốc đang di chuyển với tốc độ tới 200 hải lý/h (360 km/h) nhờ hệ thống radar trinh sát, máy định tầm laser, máy điều khiển phần tử bắn kỹ thuật số đặt trên 1 xe chỉ huy.
Thứ hai, mật độ hỏa lực lớn, dồn dập. Tốc độ bắn của một khẩu pháo đến 12 phát/phút, cho phép toàn bộ tổ hợp với biên chế đủ 6 khẩu pháo khi khai hỏa đồng thời có thể tung ra mật độ hỏa lực khủng khiếp, lên tới 72 phát/phút.
Hệ thống chỉ huy bắn trong điều kiện nhiễu cao có thể theo dõi tính toán 4 mục tiêu và xạ kích đồng thời 2 mục tiêu trong số đó. Tầm bắn tối đa 27 km. Bán kính chiến đấu hiệu quả 22 km.
Thời gian chuẩn bị xạ kích đối với mục tiêu cơ động trên biển là 1 - 2 phút. Xác xuất diệt mục tiêu là 0,8.
Xe pháo tự hành.
Tổ hợp có 1 - 2 xe phục vụ hậu cần, ăn, ngủ, sơ cứu y tế, phát điện cho tổ hợp đủ dùng trong 7 ngày với cơ số dầu dự trữ mang theo.
Thứ ba, lấp kín "vùng chết". Nếu như các tổ hợp tên lửa "bó tay" với các mục tiêu ở cự ly gần thì với A-222 Bereg lại là lợi thế, là chốt chặn cuối cùng.
Ở vòng ngoài, nếu mục tiêu xa bờ, cự ly dưới 300 km đã có tổ hợp Bation-P (với đạn tên lửa Yakhont, tầm bắn 300km) và Rubezh-ME (với đạn tên lửa Kh-35U, tầm bắn 260km).
"Bầy sói" tên lửa từ các tổ hợp này hoạt động theo phương thức "bắn và quên", sẽ tự tìm đến mục tiêu đã chỉ định, là tàu lớn của địch để đánh chìm chúng.
Gần hơn nữa, ở cự ly dưới 130 km, các mục tiêu sẽ do tổ hợp Bal-E (với đạn tên lửa Kh-35, tầm bắn 130km) đảm nhiệm với cơn mưa tên lửa .
Ở cự ly cực gần, dưới 30km, tổ hợp pháo tự hành A-222 Bereg-E sẽ làm nốt nhiệm vụ, chiến thuật "biển tàu" với hàng loạt tàu, xuồng cao tốc của đối phương sẽ bị vỡ trận.
Cấu hình cơ bản của tổ hợp pháo bờ biển di động A-222E Bereg-E
Tổ hợp pháo bờ biển di động A-222E Bereg-E được thiết kế để tiêu diệt hay chế áp lực lượng chiến đấu mặt biển hay ven biển của đối phương, ngăn chặn hỏa lực tàu chiến đấu đối phương nhắm vào lực lượng chiến đấu ven biển của ta trong tác chiến chống đổ bộ, tác chiến phòng thủ eo biển và vùng ven biển, cũng như bảo vệ tuyến hàng hải và bãi trú đậu ven bờ.
Tổ hợp có thể bắn chính xác các mục tiêu đang cơ động trên biển và trên bờ với tốc độ tới 200 hải lý/giờ (360km/h).
• Xe chỉ huy với hệ thống điều khiển hỏa lực BR-136
• 6 xe pháo tự hành
• Một hoặc hai xe phục vụ chiến đấu.
Xe chỉ huy:
Xe chỉ huy làm nhiệm vụ chỉ huy hỏa lực cho cả tổ hợp, bao gồm các trang thiết bị sau: đài ra-đa trinh sát, tổ hợp trinh sát quang tuyến truyền hình trang bị máy định tầm la-de và kính ngắm xác định mục tiêu, máy tính phần tử bắn kỹ thuật số, thiết bị kiểm tra và đánh giá kết quả xạ kích, thiết bị mô phỏng phần tử dùng huấn luyện kíp chiến đấu, máy phát điện, các thiết bị hỗ trợ chiến đấu và phục vụ kíp chiến đấu.
Hệ thống chỉ huy hỏa lực trên xe có khả năng phát hiện và tính toán phần tử bắn trong môi trường nhiễu tích cực và tiêu cực đối với 4 mục tiêu, chỉ huy tổ hợp xạ kích đồng thời 2 mục tiêu trong số đó.
Tổ hợp pháo bờ biển di động A-222 Bereg
Xe pháo tự hành
Xe pháo tự hành có thể bắn điện theo phần tử của xe chỉ huy hoặc bắn theo phần tử do hệ thống ngắm cơ hữu trên xe (kính ngắm cơ quang, máy tính đạn đạo và máy định tầm la-de) cung cấp.
Xe có máy nạp đạn bán tự động dùng cho đạn nguyên khối như đạn phá mảnh mang ngòi nổ đế, đạn phòng không mang ngòi chạm nổ, cũng như các loại đạn huấn luyện và đạn diễn tập khác.
Các xe phục vụ chiến đấu
Các xe phục vụ chiến đấu cung cấp nguồn điện cho xe chỉ huy và các xe pháo tự hành, cung cấp chỗ ăn, ngủ, nghỉ và sơ cứu cho kíp chiến đấu. Việc cấp nguồn điện cho tổ hợp do 2 máy phát đi-e-zen đảm nhiệm với cơ số dầu dự trữ đủ dùng cho 7 ngày.
Các xe của tổ hợp Bereg-E đều được thiết kế trên khung gầm xe việt dã bánh lốp MAZ-543M 8x8.
Thông số kỹ thuật cơ bản
Tầm bắn hiệu quả (km): 20
Thời gian chuẩn bị xạ kích đối với mục tiêu cơ động trên biển (với xác suất tiêu diệt bằng 0,8): 1-2 phút
Số mục tiêu có thể xạ kích đồng thời bằng tổ hợp xạ kích bất kỳ: 1-2
Cỡ nòng: 130mm
Độ dài nòng: 7020mm
Loại đạn: các loại đạn 130mm nguyên khối
Tốc tộ bắn: 12-14 phát/phút
Góc quay của pháo: -120… +120 độ
Góc tà: -5… +50 độ
Kíp trắc thủ:
Khung gầm các xe của tổ hợp: Trên khung gầm xe việt dã bánh lốp 4 cầu chủ động.

articles.title: Gigantic prehistoric snake discovered in India may have been one of the largest ever
articles.text:
Gigantic prehistoric snake discovered in India may have been one of the largest ever
- Date:
- October 14, 2026
- Source:
- Scientific Reports
- Summary:
- A massive prehistoric snake discovered in India may have rivaled the largest snake ever known. Called Vasuki indicus, the 47-million-year-old giant could have reached up to 50 feet long, making it comparable to the legendary Titanoboa. Scientists believe its enormous body made it a slow-moving ambush predator, similar to a modern anaconda.
- Share:
A colossal prehistoric snake that lived in India about 47 million years ago may have been one of the largest snakes ever to exist. Known as Vasuki indicus, the ancient reptile could have reached an extraordinary 15.2 meters (50 feet) in length, putting it in the same league as Titanoboa, the enormous extinct snake long regarded as the largest ever discovered.
The remarkable discovery, described in 2024 in the journal Scientific Reports, came from fossils unearthed in Gujarat, western India. Researchers estimate that Vasuki measured between 10.9 and 15.2 meters (36 and 50 feet) long, although its exact size remains uncertain. Its enormous body and unusual evolutionary history offer a glimpse into a time when giant snakes inhabited the warm, tropical landscapes of ancient India.
Giant Snake Fossils Unearthed in India
Paleontologists Debajit Datta and Sunil Bajpai of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee identified the species from fossils recovered at the Panandhro Lignite Mine in Kutch, Gujarat. The remains date to the Middle Eocene, a period roughly 47 million years ago when Earth's climate was considerably warmer than it is today.
The researchers examined 27 fossilized vertebrae, the individual bones that make up a snake's backbone. Many were remarkably well preserved, and some remained connected in their original arrangement. The bones appear to have belonged to a fully grown animal.
The species was named Vasuki indicus in honor of Vasuki, the mythical serpent associated with the Hindu deity Shiva, who is traditionally depicted with the snake wrapped around his neck. The second part of the name refers to India, where the fossils were discovered.
How Big Was This Prehistoric Snake?
Although the scientists did not recover a complete skeleton, the preserved backbone provides important clues about the snake's enormous proportions.
Individual vertebrae measured between 37.5 and 62.7 millimeters (1.48 and 2.47 inches) long and between 62.4 and 111.4 millimeters (2.46 and 4.39 inches) wide. Their unusually broad shape suggests that Vasuki possessed a thick, cylindrical body capable of supporting tremendous weight.
To estimate its total length, the researchers compared the fossilized bones with vertebrae from living snakes whose body lengths are known. Two different methods produced estimates ranging from 10.9 to 12.2 meters (36 to 40 feet) and 14.5 to 15.2 meters (48 to 50 feet).
Those measurements place Vasuki among the largest snakes ever identified. Its estimated length rivals that of Titanoboa, the giant snake that inhabited what is now Colombia approximately 60 million years ago and is thought to have reached around 13 meters (43 feet).
However, the researchers caution that their calculations involve considerable uncertainty. Different methods can produce substantially different estimates, particularly when scientists must reconstruct an extinct animal using an incomplete backbone. It remains unclear whether Vasuki actually exceeded Titanoboa in length.
A Massive Predator That Likely Hunted by Ambush
Despite its intimidating size, Vasuki probably was not a particularly fast or agile hunter.
The researchers suggest that its enormous body and distinctive vertebral structure would have favored relatively slow movement. Rather than actively chasing prey, the snake may have relied on ambush tactics, remaining concealed until another animal came within striking distance.
Its hunting behavior could have resembled that of modern anacondas and large pythons, which can overpower prey through constriction. These snakes use their muscular bodies to tighten around captured animals, interfering with circulation until the prey dies.
Scientists suspect Vasuki may have hunted in a similar way, although its precise diet and hunting behavior cannot be determined from the surviving fossils.
Its anatomy also suggests that the snake may have spent much of its time on land or in shallow, swampy environments, rather than living exclusively in water. The ancient landscape surrounding the fossil site contained wetlands and marshes that could have provided suitable habitat for an enormous ambush predator.
Ancient India's Warm Climate May Have Helped Snakes Grow Enormous
The discovery also raises questions about why some prehistoric snakes reached sizes far beyond those of most species alive today.
During the Middle Eocene, the region where Vasuki lived experienced tropical conditions, with average temperatures estimated at approximately 28 degrees Celsius (82 degrees Fahrenheit).
Snakes are ectothermic animals, meaning they depend heavily on external sources of heat to regulate their body temperature. Warm environments can support the activity, digestion, and growth of large reptiles, potentially helping explain why exceptionally large snakes appeared during some of Earth's warmer periods.
However, temperature alone does not determine how large a snake can become. Food availability, suitable habitat, evolutionary history, and other environmental factors also influence body size.
A Lost Lineage of Giant Snakes That Spread Across Continents
Beyond its extraordinary size, Vasuki provides evidence of an ancient branch of snake evolution.
The species belonged to Madtsoiidae, an extinct family of snakes that survived for roughly 100 million years, from the Late Cretaceous to the Late Pleistocene. Members of this group occupied regions including India, Africa, Europe, South America, and Australia.
Unlike modern anacondas and pythons, Vasuki represented a separate evolutionary lineage within this long-extinct family.
The researchers found that its closest relatives included Madtsoia pisdurensis, a fossil snake from ancient India, and Gigantophis garstini, another large prehistoric snake known from North Africa.
These relationships suggest that a lineage of giant madtsoiid snakes originated on the Indian subcontinent before spreading into other parts of the world.
As India moved northward and collided with Asia around 50 million years ago, changing geographic connections may have allowed these snakes to disperse through southern Eurasia, including southern Europe, and eventually into Africa during the Eocene, approximately 56 to 34 million years ago.
Later Fossil Discoveries Reveal an Ancient World Filled With Snakes
Research published in 2025 has added important context to the discovery of Vasuki.
In a study published in the Journal of Paleontology, Datta and Bajpai described additional fossil snakes from Eocene deposits in western India. Their findings revealed a surprisingly diverse community of ancient reptiles, including aquatic snakes, another large member of the madtsoiid family, and other extinct snake groups.
Among the discoveries was Pterosphenus rannensis, an ancient aquatic snake species that adds to scientists' understanding of how these reptiles evolved and spread.
The researchers also identified another madtsoiid snake that appears to have shared a marshy environment with Vasuki. This suggests that the giant predator was part of a broader community of snakes occupying different ecological roles, rather than an isolated evolutionary oddity.
Evidence from the fossil deposits indicates that some of these snakes inhabited tidal environments, while others occupied swamps and marshes. Together, the discoveries paint a more detailed picture of the complex ecosystems that existed in India tens of millions of years ago.
What Modern Anacondas Reveal About Giant Snakes
Additional evidence about snake gigantism emerged from a separate 2025 study published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.
Researchers examining fossilized anaconda vertebrae from Venezuela found that these enormous snakes had already evolved large bodies by approximately 12.4 million years ago. Ancient anacondas reached estimated lengths of around 5.2 meters (17 feet), comparable to the size of many living anacondas.
The findings suggest that anacondas maintained their impressive size for millions of years, even as climates and ecosystems changed. They also show that prehistoric snakes did not necessarily grow larger simply because the planet was warmer.
Although anacondas are evolutionarily distinct from Vasuki, the research offers a useful comparison for understanding how different snake lineages became giants and adapted to their environments.
For Vasuki indicus, the full story remains incomplete. Its precise size, appearance, and behavior are still uncertain, but the fossil evidence establishes it as an extraordinary example of prehistoric gigantism.
Together with later discoveries from the same region, the ancient snake is helping scientists reconstruct a largely forgotten world in which massive serpents occupied the tropical landscapes of India.

articles.title: New knee arthritis treatment delivers lasting pain relief without surgery
articles.text:
New knee arthritis treatment delivers lasting pain relief without surgery
- Date:
- October 14, 2026
- Source:
- Radiological Society of North America
- Summary:
- A promising new treatment for knee arthritis uses tiny, dissolvable particles to block abnormal blood vessels, easing inflammation and pain without joint replacement surgery. In a study of 194 patients, 80% experienced clinically meaningful pain relief lasting at least 12 months.
- Share:
A minimally invasive procedure that targets abnormal blood vessels in the knee could provide lasting relief for people struggling with osteoarthritis, offering a potential alternative to joint replacement surgery.
In a study involving 194 patients, researchers found that a treatment using tiny particles that dissolve within hours was associated with substantial reductions in knee pain and improvements in mobility. The benefits persisted for at least 12 months, with 80% of patients assessed at the one-year follow-up reporting clinically meaningful pain relief.
The approach, known as genicular artery embolization, aims to interrupt the inflammation and abnormal blood vessel growth that contribute to chronic knee pain. Rather than replacing the damaged joint, doctors use a thin catheter to deliver microscopic particles directly into specific blood vessels.
The findings, published in the journal Radiology, suggest that this technique could provide another option for patients who have exhausted conventional treatments but cannot or do not want to undergo knee replacement surgery.
Why Knee Arthritis Is So Difficult To Treat
Osteoarthritis is the world's most common form of arthritis and a major cause of disability. According to the World Health Organization, knee osteoarthritis affects more than 365 million adults worldwide.
The condition develops as cartilage, the protective tissue that cushions the ends of bones, gradually deteriorates. But osteoarthritis involves more than cartilage damage. Inflammation within the joint, changes in surrounding tissues, and increased sensitivity of pain signaling nerves can all contribute to persistent discomfort.
For many people, the consequences extend far beyond occasional knee pain. Everyday activities such as walking, climbing stairs, exercising, or standing for extended periods can become increasingly difficult.
Treatments typically begin with physical therapy, medication, and injections into the affected joint. When these approaches stop providing adequate relief, knee replacement surgery may eventually be considered. However, surgery is not appropriate or desirable for everyone.
"For many patients with knee osteoarthritis, there is a real treatment gap today," said Florian Nima Fleckenstein, M.D., deputy head of Interventional Radiology Campus Mitte, Charité -- Universitätsmedizin Berlin. "Conservative measures such as intra-articular injections no longer provide sufficient relief, but joint replacement is not an option for medical or personal reasons."
A Different Way To Fight Knee Arthritis Pain
The treatment being investigated, genicular artery embolization (GAE), approaches knee arthritis from an unusual direction. Instead of focusing directly on damaged cartilage, it targets the abnormal blood vessels that develop around an inflamed joint.
These vessels can form within and around the synovium, a thin membrane lining the inside of the joint. As the vessels multiply, they can contribute to inflammation and encourage the growth of sensory nerves involved in transmitting pain.
GAE is designed to interrupt this process by reducing blood flow through the abnormal vessels while preserving the knee's normal circulation.
During the procedure, an interventional radiologist inserts a thin catheter into an artery and carefully guides it toward the affected blood vessels. Tiny particles are then injected to block selected vessels, with the goal of reducing inflammation and pain.
The technique is called superselective embolization because doctors target specific small arteries rather than blocking circulation throughout the joint. It does not require an open surgical incision or replacement of the knee.
Researchers have previously investigated both temporary blocking agents and permanent microscopic particles. Each approach has potential drawbacks, including differences in how precisely the particles can be delivered and how long they remain inside the blood vessels.
For this study, the team examined rapidly resorbable, gelatin-based microspheres. These precisely sized, spherical particles are engineered to dissolve within hours, potentially combining the advantages of temporary agents with the controlled delivery of permanent microspheres.
"GAE is a whole new treatment regimen that targets abnormal hypervascularity around the joint and, in turn, modulates the pathological neurovascular environment," Dr. Fleckenstein said.
Hypervascularity refers to an unusually high concentration of blood vessels. The pathological neurovascular environment describes the abnormal interactions between those vessels and pain signaling nerves in the affected tissue.
"By reducing both inflammation and pain, GAE with resorbable microspheres may be the first procedure that alters the course of the disease, slowing its progression."
Whether the procedure can actually slow osteoarthritis progression remains an open question. Although reducing inflammation could theoretically influence the disease, the study did not demonstrate that GAE prevents cartilage deterioration or reverses existing joint damage.
Nearly 200 Patients Underwent the Procedure
To evaluate the approach, researchers conducted a prospective single-center study involving 194 patients with osteoarthritis-related knee pain. The participants included 114 women and 80 men, with a median age of 69 years and a median body mass index of 28.4.
All had continued to experience symptoms despite at least three months of conventional care, including physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medications, and injections into the knee.
"We believe these results carry real weight because they come from real-world data," Dr. Fleckenstein said. "With this broad, inclusive study design, our participants are exactly the patients that physicians encounter every day in their practices."
The procedures took place between July and November 2024. Forty-five participants (23%) had osteoarthritis affecting both knees and received two separate treatments, with the second performed within four weeks of the first.
Altogether, the researchers carried out 239 GAE procedures.
Doctors used real-time X-ray imaging, known as fluoroscopy, to guide the catheter and deliver the particles to the targeted arteries. All 239 procedures were technically successful, meaning the intended blood vessels were successfully treated.
The safety findings were also encouraging. No moderate or severe adverse events were recorded, and mild, temporary complications occurred in 6.7% of procedures.
These included brief skin discoloration near the treated area and one superficial collection of blood near the catheter insertion site. All resolved without lasting complications.
Knee Arthritis Pain Dropped and Stayed Lower for a Year
The researchers monitored pain, movement, and quality of life before treatment and at several intervals afterward. Assessments were conducted at six weeks, three months, six months, and 12 months. An orthopedic surgeon also examined patients in person at the six-month follow-up.
Participant retention remained relatively high throughout the study. Follow-up rates were 94% at six weeks (183/194), 89% at three months (172/194), 89% at six months (171/194), and 79% at 12 months (154/194).
The most striking finding was the sustained reduction in knee pain.
Using the Numeric Rating Scale (a 0-to-10 measure of pain intensity), median pain scores fell from 7 before treatment to 4 after six weeks. By six months, the median score had declined to 3, and it remained at that level at the 12-month follow-up.
That represents a reduction of more than half from the original median pain score, with benefits that were still apparent a full year after treatment.
"In our cohort, we saw a significant drop in pain and a significant increase in function, including sports and recreation and daily activity," Dr. Fleckenstein said. "Most importantly, their quality of life significantly increased."
Patients Also Reported Better Mobility and Quality of Life
The improvements extended beyond pain reduction. Researchers used the Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score, a standardized questionnaire that evaluates how knee problems affect symptoms, mobility, recreation, and everyday life.
Across all five areas assessed, patients reported meaningful progress during the year following treatment.
Median scores for daily activities increased from 53 to 71.5, suggesting that routine movements such as walking and climbing stairs became easier. Sports and recreation scores climbed from 15 to 36, indicating improvements in more physically demanding activities.
Scores measuring osteoarthritis symptoms rose from 51 to 68, while the pain category improved from 44 to 65 (where 0 indicates extreme knee pain and 100 indicates no pain at all).
Quality of life scores also increased substantially, rising from 19 before treatment to 40 after 12 months.
To determine whether these changes were large enough to matter to patients, the researchers applied established thresholds for clinically meaningful improvement.
Previous studies have identified a reduction of at least 2.0 points on the Numeric Rating Scale and an increase of at least 10 points in the Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score categories as meaningful improvements.
These thresholds are known as the minimum clinically important difference. In simple terms, they distinguish changes that are likely to be noticeable in daily life from smaller statistical differences that may have little practical significance.
At 12 months, 80% of participants who completed the pain assessment exceeded the clinically meaningful improvement threshold.
"Our study demonstrates that GAE using rapidly resorbable gelatin-based microspheres is a safe, minimally invasive therapy that provides meaningful pain relief and functional improvement in participants with osteoarthritis-related knee symptoms for at least 12 months," Dr. Fleckenstein said. "By embolizing the pathological vessels, we're able to normalize the vessel structure -- and, in turn, the neuronal structure of the knee."
What Other Studies Reveal About Knee Artery Embolization
The results add to a growing body of evidence investigating whether blocking abnormal knee blood vessels can offer sustained relief from osteoarthritis.
A randomized study published in Clinical Radiology in 2026 provided encouraging findings. Researchers compared GAE combined with standard care against standard care alone in 50 patients. After one year, pain scores had improved by 72.7% in the embolization group, compared with 24.2% in the standard care group. The treated patients also reported better knee function.
However, that study used polyvinyl alcohol particles rather than the dissolving gelatin particles examined by Fleckenstein's team. It also did not include a sham procedure, making it difficult to separate the treatment's physical effects from patients' expectations.
Other research has raised important questions about how much of the improvement is caused by embolization itself.
A randomized, sham-controlled study published in European Radiology in April 2026 followed 58 patients for 12 months. Both the GAE and sham treatment groups experienced sustained reductions in pain, but researchers found no statistically significant difference between them. MRI examinations also failed to identify a significant reduction in joint inflammation attributable to embolization.
Similarly, an analysis appearing in the September 2026 issue of the European Journal of Radiology examined 22 studies involving 633 patients. Although pain scores often improved substantially after treatment, the researchers found no statistically significant advantage over sham procedures when results from three randomized trials were combined.
A separate June 2026 analysis of 45 studies involving 2,205 patients also documented improvements in pain and function, but judged the overall certainty of the evidence to be low or very low.
Together, these findings suggest that GAE is associated with promising improvements, particularly in observational studies, but more rigorous trials are needed to establish how much benefit comes directly from blocking the blood vessels.
Could This Treatment Help Patients Avoid Knee Replacement?
Despite the remaining uncertainties, researchers and medical specialists are increasingly exploring GAE as a possible option for patients who have limited alternatives.
In a 2026 position statement, the Society of Interventional Radiology supported offering the procedure to appropriately selected patients whose symptoms persist despite conservative treatment, particularly those who cannot undergo or wish to delay knee replacement surgery.
The society also emphasized the importance of specialist training, careful patient selection, and continued clinical trials to establish the treatment's effectiveness and long-term safety.
The study led by Fleckenstein provides particularly valuable information about rapidly resorbable gelatin microspheres. With nearly 200 participants, it represented the largest published clinical investigation of this specific approach at the time.
Still, because the study did not include an untreated or sham treatment comparison group, it cannot establish how much of the observed improvement resulted directly from the procedure. The researchers also did not evaluate whether the treatment slows cartilage loss or prevents patients from eventually needing joint replacement.
Longer follow-up and larger controlled trials will be essential to determine how durable the benefits are, which patients respond best, and whether dissolving particles offer advantages over other embolization materials.
For patients whose knee arthritis continues to interfere with everyday life despite medication, therapy, and injections, the approach nevertheless represents an increasingly studied possibility.
"This lets us speak about safety and efficacy with real confidence," Dr. Fleckenstein said. "For the right patient, it can mean lasting relief from a single, minimally invasive procedure -- a meaningful new option between injections and joint replacement."

articles.title: Lốc xoáy có nguồn gốc từ đâu?
articles.text:
Người ta cho rằng khi không khí ở lớp bên trên lạnh đè lên lớp không khí nóng ở phía dưới, không khí nóng sẽ bị cưỡng bức chuyển động lên rất mạnh.
Lốc xoáy phát triển từ một cơn dông, thường từ ổ dông rất mạnh hay siêu mạnh, nên ở đâu có dông dữ dội là ở đó có thể có lốc xoáy, song cũng may là nó rất hiếm. Cũng có khi nó sinh ra từ một dải gió giật mạnh (được gọi là những đường tố) hay từ một cơn bão. Người ta cho rằng khi không khí ở lớp bên trên lạnh đè lên lớp không khí nóng ở phía dưới, không khí nóng sẽ bị cưỡng bức chuyển động lên rất mạnh. Nhưng khi lốc xoáy xảy ra trên mặt nước thì thường lại không thấy đối lưu và cũng không thấy sự khác biệt nhiệt độ giữa các lớp. Vì vậy nguyên nhân lốc xoáy con người vẫn chưa hoàn toàn hiểu được hết.
Tuy vậy, phần lớn lốc xoáy được hình thành từ một dạng mây dông đặc biệt là mây dông tích điện. Một đám mây có thể kéo dài trong vài giờ, xoáy tròn trong vùng có đường kính từ 10 đến 16 km, di chuyển hàng trăm dặm và sinh ra vô số ống hút khổng lồ.
Nguồn gốc của chúng là vùng khí hậu có luồng khí nóng đi lên và luồng khí lạnh đi xuống. Đầu tiên là quá trình tương tác giữa cơn dông có chiều lên trên và gió. Sự tương tác này sẽ làm cho tầng khí nóng ở dưới di chuyển lên trên và xoay tròn trong không trung. Tiếp đó là sự phát triển của dòng khí lạnh di chuyển theo hướng đi xuống mặt đất ở phía bên kia của cơn bão. Vận tốc của dòng khí đi xuống có thể lớn hơn 160km/h.
Lốc xoáy kết hợp sét.
Đường kính của lốc xoáy có thể thay đổi từ vài chục mét cho tới vài km Nhưng đa số các lốc xoáy có đường kính vào khoảng 50m. Trên đường di chuyển nó có thể cuốn theo (rồi ném xuống ở một khoảng cách sau đó) hoặc phá hủy mọi thứ, kể cả những nhà gạch xây kiên cố, nên lốc xoáy cũng là hiện tượng khí tượng đặc biệt nguy hiểm. Âm thanh lốc xoáy thường là tiếng đùng đùng liên tục, giống như âm thanh khi tàu hỏa sắp đến. Đôi khi lốc xoáy tạo ra tiếng ồn lớn như tiếng thác nước đổ hoặc tiếng ồn mở cửa kính ô tô khi xe chạy cực nhanh. Nhìn từ xa lốc xoáy có thể có màu đen hoặc trắng, tùy thuộc những thứ mà nó cuốn theo. Khi lốc xoáy xuất hiện ở trên đại dương, hình thành nên vòi rồng, thường hút bụi nước lên cao tạo thành các cây nước (waterspouts) nặng hàng chục tấn.
Trong giai đoạn từ năm 2000 đến 2013, chỉ tính riêng ở Hoa Kỳ, đã ghi nhận nhiều trận lốc xoáy gây thiệt hại nặng nề về người và tài sản.
Những trận lốc xoáy được ghi nhận từ năm 2000 đến 2013.

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.text:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness
Published in the journal Cognition, the study was led by Dr. Louis Longin of LMU's Chair of Philosophy of Mind, working alongside Dr. Bahador Bahrami, Professor Ophelia Deroy, and other researchers.
"Whereas previous studies have typically asked general questions about whether AI actually has mental states, our study is the first to directly compare how people attribute the same mental states to AI and humans behaving in exactly the same way, under identical circumstances," says Longin.
"We may be using mental terms to refer to AI, but this may only be because we lack better words," says Ophelia Deroy, philosopher and a senior author of the study. "After all, AI is trained to act and speak like a human, so these descriptions seem natural."
To investigate how people judge consciousness, the researchers conducted experiments involving nearly 1,100 participants. One group read brief descriptions of artificial agents that showed different levels of responsiveness to their environments. For example, some agents reacted to sounds or recognized the emotional states of others.
Another group encountered the same situations, except the characters were described as humans rather than AI systems. Participants then evaluated how conscious or aware each character seemed to be of its surroundings.
A Surprising Gap Between Human and AI Consciousness
The experiments revealed that responsiveness influenced how participants judged both humans and artificial intelligence. Characters that reacted more actively to their surroundings were generally considered more conscious and more aware.
However, a striking difference emerged when participants evaluated consciousness specifically. Even the most responsive AI was rated as less conscious than the least responsive human. In other words, identical behavior did not lead people to assign the same level of consciousness to humans and machines.
The results changed considerably when participants were asked about awareness instead. For this characteristic, judgments of humans and AI followed largely similar patterns, suggesting that people interpret awareness and consciousness in fundamentally different ways.
"There is a growing worry in public discussion that people will see AI behaving in a human-like way and start treating these systems as if they had human-like mental states," says Longin, lead author of the study. "We found something much more nuanced: People are quite willing to say that an AI notices things and is aware of its surroundings. But they clearly draw a line when it comes to the term 'consciousness'. People consistently attribute less consciousness to AI than humans -- even when their behavior is identical."
Although people sometimes describe AI as conscious when discussing its actions, the findings indicate that they still distinguish between artificial systems and human minds.
Why One Word Changes How We Perceive AI
The researchers believe the difference between consciousness and awareness offers an important insight into how people understand artificial intelligence.
Awareness is a relatively neutral term that can describe an agent's ability to detect and respond to information in its environment. Consciousness, however, carries deeper implications about subjective experience and what it means to have an inner mental life.
Because awareness focuses more directly on observable behavior, people appear comfortable applying it to both humans and AI. Consciousness carries a different meaning, leading people to judge the two much less similarly.
The findings also highlight why the language used to discuss artificial intelligence matters, particularly as AI systems become increasingly capable of producing convincing human behavior.
"Our study teaches us lessons for how we communicate about AI," says Bahador Bahrami, who is also a senior author of the study and an expert in social neuroscience. "Companies and journalists often reach for hyped descriptions of AI models, and credit them with intentions, plans, or even moral conscience and hesitation. What our study shows is that everyday judgments are much more discriminating: People do not simply put AI and humans on the same mental scale. But the boundary also depends on which terms we use. For more neutral descriptors such as 'awareness', the distinction can largely disappear. That makes our choice of language important."
Story Source:
Materials provided by Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Louis Longin, Jurgis Karpus, Nadine Meertens, Bahador Bahrami, Ophelia Deroy. AI is not as conscious as humans: Essentialism in mental state attributions to artificial systems. Cognition, 2027; 278: 106733 DOI: 10.1016/j.cognition.2026.106733

articles.title: Tại sao không thể so sánh độ khó xây dựng của các kim tự tháp với Vạn Lý Trường Thành?
articles.text:
Dưới góc độ khối lượng công trình, Vạn Lý Trường Thành gấp nhiều lần các kim tự tháp, tuy trọng lượng của mỗi viên gạch nhỏ hơn nhiều nhưng khối lượng tổng thể lại rất lớn.
Người xây dựng Vạn Lý Trường Thành nổi tiếng là Tần Thủy Hoàng. Sử sách ghi lại rằng sau khi Tần Thủy Hoàng thống nhất sáu vương quốc, chính Vạn Lý Trường Thành đã liên kết Triệu, Hán, v.v..., và được biết đến như một tuyến phòng thủ hoàn chỉnh phía bắc. Vạn Lý Trường Thành thời nhà Minh vẫn được xây dựng, với thời gian xây dựng kéo dài 2000 năm.
Khó có thể so sánh Vạn Lý Trường Thành với Kim Tự Tháp.
Vào khoảng năm 3100 trước Công nguyên, nhà nước Ai Cập cổ đại thống nhất ban đầu được thành lập. Các vị vua Ai Cập cổ đại, còn được gọi là pharaoh, có quyền lực tối cao và được xem như hóa thân của các vị thần. Họ đã tự xây cho mình những kim tự tháp lăng tẩm khổng lồ. Pharaoh tin rằng "cuộc sống chỉ là một thời gian ngắn, và sau khi chết là một sự tận hưởng vĩnh viễn".
Vì vậy, người Ai Cập coi âm phủ là nơi tiếp nối của cuộc sống trần gian, khi còn sống người Ai Cập cổ đại họ tự tin chuẩn bị cho mình một ngôi mộ để có được cuộc sống vĩnh hằng sau khi chết. Các Pharaoh sẽ dành nhiều năm, thậm chí nhiều thập kỷ để xây dựng lăng mộ của riêng mình, những kim tự tháp kiến trúc vĩ đại của hành tinh. Việc xây dựng kim tự tháp Khufu lớn nhất ở Ai Cập mất khoảng 30 năm.
Theo quan điểm hiện đại, việc xây dựng các kim tự tháp của Ai Cập cách đây 5, 6 nghìn năm quả thực là rất khó, nếu ở Ai Cập có hơn 110 kim tự tháp lớn nhỏ thì tổng quy mô xây dựng có thể so sánh với Vạn Lý Trường Thành. Các kim tự tháp Ai Cập chỉ khó hơn một chút so với lăng của các hoàng đế Trung Quốc cổ đại với cấu trúc bằng bùn và đá.
Khu vực đặt các kim tự tháp nói chung là dọc theo sông Nile. Sông Nile là con sông lớn nhất ở Châu Phi và có chức năng giao thông quan trọng. Vật liệu đá ở xa cũng có thể được vận chuyển bằng sông Nile nên tiết kiệm được rất nhiều nhân lực và vật lực. Kim tự tháp lớn nhất được xây dựng kể từ khi Khufu lên ngôi, kéo dài chỉ vài thập kỷ.
Việc xây dựng Vạn Lý Trường Thành không phải trên địa hình bằng phẳng mà ở trên núi cao, chức năng là trấn thủ kinh thành. Công năng chính của Vạn Lý Trường Thành là chống giặc ngoại xâm, phần lớn được xây dựng ven sông, núi, cứ cách 1.000m lại có một tháp báo hiệu, bên trong có quân lính đóng. Nếu có giặc ngoại xâm thì ban ngày đốt khói, ban đêm đốt lửa, thời cổ đại đã tận dụng triệt để các điều kiện tự nhiên để truyền tin.
Vạn Lý Trường Thành trải dài 10.000km, hầu hết chúng được xây dựng trên sườn núi phía bắc. Người ta ước tính rằng nếu gạch và đá của Vạn Lý Trường Thành được chất thành một bức tường thành có chiều rộng là một mét, thì chiều dài của Vạn Lý Trường Thành có thể quay quanh Trái đất.

articles.title: California redwoods are struggling in the heat — and it's not clear how much damage is being done
articles.text:
California redwoods are struggling in the heat — and it's not clear how much damage is being done
When temperatures rise, California redwoods slow down their rate of photosynthesis, a discovery that could have implications for the long-term survival of the iconic species.
When temperatures spike, California redwoods slow down photosynthesis, new research has found. This finding has serious implications for the long-term survival of the iconic trees in a warming world, and their role in storing carbon from the atmosphere.
California redwood (Sequoia sempervirens) forests are among the largest aboveground carbon stores on the planet. These towering trees are native to central and northern California, and evolved to take advantage of the region's historically mild weather. In recent decades, their range has contracted significantly. But climate change is threatening the health and function of these forests.
The region has seen significant warming in recent decades, and faces more frequent extreme heat days, with temperatures spiking above 100 degrees Fahrenheit (37 degrees Celsius). Now, in a new study, published Sept. 22 in the journal JGR Biogeosciences, a team of researchers has shown that California's renowned redwoods are struggling to photosynthesize in the heat.
Photosynthesis is the process used by plants, algae and some bacteria to turn sunlight into energy. It chemically converts carbon dioxide and water into sugars and oxygen.
"These trees adapted to grow in really temperate environments, so no one had really looked at the impact of heat on photosynthesis," study first author Lily Klinek, a doctoral candidate in the Plant Optics Lab at the University of California, Davis, told Live Science.
From 2022 to 2024, Klinek and colleagues measured how the leaves of redwoods in Garcia River Forest in Mendocino County responded to the heat. Once or twice a month, the researchers took three different California redwood leaf samples and measured their fluorescence and temperature.
A plant's molecules can use absorbed light in three ways: for photosynthesis, dissipated as heat, or reflected as light (florescence). Fluorescence is a proxy measurement to understand photosynthesis in the plant, Klinek said.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
The researchers wrapped a fourth leaf in tinfoil for 20 minutes to put it in a state of "rest" before taking the same measurements. "When they're in a state of rest, we expose them to a pulse of light that’s in the wavelength they would use for photosynthesis to see what would be their maximum photosynthetic rate," Klinek said.
They found that on hot days, the leaves exposed to sunlight were up to 18 degrees Fahrenheit (10 degrees Celsius) hotter than the air temperature. "That's a huge difference and indicates that the leaves are stressed to the point where they can't thermoregulate effectively," Klinek said.
Many plants' leaves manage their temperature and photosynthesis by opening or closing their stomata, which are tiny pores on their surface. These stomata (from the Greek word for mouth) regulate the amount of carbon dioxide entering the plant, and how much oxygen and water vapor it releases. Lower carbon dioxide intake leads to reduced photosynthesis, meaning the plant has less energy.
The large differences between air and redwood leaf temperatures suggest that the leaves had closed their stomata to avoid losing water from evaporation during hot conditions and consequently overheated, Klinek said.
To further investigate the impact of heat on leaf physiology, the researchers took California redwood leaf samples back to the laboratory and exposed them to a range of temperatures while they were in water. Despite their access to water, the leaves still photosynthesized less as they got hotter, even though their stomata were open, Klinek said.
This shows that heat imposes direct limitations on redwood photosynthetical capacity, rather than indirectly decreasing that capacity by causing stomatal closure, the researchers wrote. The finding indicates that redwoods' ability to photosynthesise and store carbon will decrease as temperatures rise.
"It is not only stomatal closure that is causing reduced photosynthesis," Lucy Rowland, an ecologist at the University of Exeter in the U.K. who was not involved in the study, told Live Science in an email. "These trees are already suffering from the direct effects of heat on their photosynthetic systems."
Related stories
- The central Pacific Ocean just broke a temperature record. Experts say it might signal a new kind of El Niño.
- Aspen trees provide a natural buffer against wildfires, even as fire season intensifies, study shows
- 'A worrying snapshot': Satellite image shows large patches of open water less than 40 miles from the North Pole
The finding has serious implications for the future of redwoods and similar plants. "The points at which this damage becomes irreversible remains really poorly understood, but is something which is really essential to understand if we want to predict how our future climate is going to impact plants," she said.
The next step in Klinek's research is to move beyond leaf physiology to understand these thresholds on the trees and their ecosystems as a whole.
"We're not sure to what extent the effect that we saw is a reversible stress response and if they are sustaining damage from this constant stress," she said. Researchers need more data to "really get a better sense, beyond the leaf scale, how these ecosystems are responding to heat and drought," she added.
Klinek, L., Au, J., Rodriguez‐Caton, M., Rao, M. P., Fety, L., Koch, G. W., & Magney, T. S. (2026). Summer heat stress downregulates photochemistry in Coast Redwoods. Journal of Geophysical Research Biogeosciences, 131(9). https://doi.org/10.1029/2026jg010052
Sarah Wild is a British-South African freelance science journalist. She has written about particle physics, cosmology and everything in between. She studied physics, electronics and English literature at Rhodes University, South Africa, and later read for an MSc Medicine in bioethics.
Since she started perpetrating journalism for a living, she's written books, won awards, and run national science desks. Her work has appeared in Nature, Science, Scientific American, and The Observer, among others. In 2017 she won a gold AAAS Kavli for her reporting on forensics in South Africa.

articles.title: Giải mã bí ẩn vượn cái tự mang thai tại vườn thú Nhật Bản
articles.text:
Một sở thú tại miền Nam Nhật Bản đã vô cùng bối rối trong việc đi tìm lời giải thích cho bí ẩn kéo dài suốt hai năm qua: bằng cách nào mà Momo, cô vượn bị nhốt một mình trong lồng sắt tại đây lại có thể mang thai?
Cô vượn tay trắng 12 tuổi sống cô quạnh một mình và hoàn toàn không hề kết bạn với bất kỳ tri kỷ nào. Hiển nhiên là hàng xóm của cô phải bao gồm một vài cá thể vượn đực, thế nhưng chuồng của chúng được ngăn cách nhau bởi các thanh chắn kiên cố và hàng rào lưới mắt cáo lởm chởm, nên kịch bản Momo và một con vượn đực khác có thể vượt qua hai lớp bảo vệ để giao phối nhanh chóng bị những người quản lý vườn thú bác bỏ. Năm 2021, Momo lâm bồn và hạ sinh một bé vượn đực (chưa được đặt tên) với mái tóc đen cùng bộ lông trắng bao phủ gọn gàng quanh khuôn mặt.
Momo cùng con
Bí ẩn cuối cùng cũng đã có lời giải đáp nhờ vào sự trợ giúp của các xét nghiệm DNA. Theo đó, những người quản lý vườn thú ở tỉnh Nagasaki đã xác định được cha của chú vượn con, đồng thời cũng tìm ra cách cha mẹ của chú gặp gỡ.
Sau khi nhờ một nhà nghiên cứu tiến hành phân tích DNA trong mẫu phân và tóc thu thập được vào năm ngoái từ sáu cá thể vượn: Momo và con, cùng bốn con vượn đực có tiềm năng sáng giá trong cuộc đua làm “cha đứa trẻ”, hôm thứ Ba vừa rồi Vườn bách thảo và Sở thú Kujukushima đã công bố danh tính của vượn cha: Itoh - một con vượn nhanh nhẹn 34 tuổi.
“Phải mất đến hai năm để chúng tôi có thể giải mã bí ẩn này, đơn giản vì chúng tôi không thể dễ dàng lại gần để thu thập các mẫu DNA - Momo rất bảo vệ con”, Giám đốc sở thú Jun Yamano cho biết.
Đã xác định được vượn cha rồi, nhưng vẫn còn đó một câu hỏi nhức nhối không kém: nếu Momo chưa bao giờ tiếp xúc trực tiếp với Itoh, vậy bằng cách nào mà cô vượn này lại có thai ngay từ đầu?
Sở thú không có những bằng chứng tường minh kiểu như một đoạn phim giám sát, nhưng Yamano suy đoán rằng điểm tiếp xúc của hai cá thể vượn có lẽ là một lỗ hổng trên tường có đường kính chỉ 9mm.
Tại sở thú, Momo và Itoh thay phiên nhau trình diễn trước khách ghé thăm vào buổi sáng và buổi chiều trong cùng một khu vực triển lãm nằm ngay trước lồng của Momo; hai không gian này được ngăn cách chỉ bởi một vách ngăn - một tấm ván đục lỗ - với mong muốn ngăn không cho những con vượn gần gũi với nhau.
Vậy nhưng, quả thật nếu không muốn thì sẽ tìm lí do, còn nếu muốn thì sẽ tìm cách.
“Chúng tôi nghĩ rằng rất có thể vào một trong những ngày mà Itoh được nhốt trong khu vực triển lãm, nó và Momo đã tiến hành giao phối, thông qua một trong những cái lỗ trên tấm vách ngăn”, Yamano nói.
Và Itoh, cha đứa bé
Những thói quen giao phối kiểu như vậy chưa từng được ghi nhận trước đây, Yamano cho biết. Thông thường, sở thú tiến hành ghép đôi cho vượn sau hàng loạt phép thử và sai để những con vượn làm quen và thực sự cảm thấy gần gũi với nhau.
Trong tự nhiên, loài vượn lựa chọn bạn tình dựa trên những tiêu chí về ngoại hình, hành vi xã hội và giọng hát, chẳng hạn như thông qua những bài hát phức tạp mà chúng thể hiện. Sở thú không bật mí gì thêm về phương thức Itoh đã dùng để “cưa cẩm” Momo (nếu có).
Kể từ khi bí ẩn được giải mã, Yamano cho biết sở thú mong muốn sẽ chuyển Itoh đến sống cùng Momo và con của chúng.
“Cả ba sẽ phải làm quen với nhau trước, nhưng hi vọng chúng sẽ sống với nhau như một gia đình”, Giám đốc sở thú nói.
Để ngăn ngừa câu chuyện tương tự có thể tái diễn, hiện sở thú đã thay thế tấm ván đục lỗ nói trên bằng một hàng rào chắn hoàn toàn không có bất kỳ khe hở nào, Yamano cho biết thêm.

articles.title: A planet 320 light-years away confirms what scientists long suspected
articles.text:
A planet 320 light-years away confirms what scientists long suspected
A scorching-hot planet 320 light-years away has confirmed a long-held assumption about planet formation, offering a powerful new clue in the search for habitable worlds.
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy (AURA)
- Summary:
- Astronomers have discovered that a scorching-hot planet 320 light-years away shares a striking chemical similarity with its host star, providing the first direct evidence for a fundamental assumption about planet formation. The breakthrough could help scientists predict what distant rocky planets are made of and identify worlds with conditions favorable for life.
- Share:
A scorching hot planet nearly 320 light-years from Earth has provided the first direct evidence for a fundamental assumption about how planets form. Astronomers discovered that WASP-189b shares an important chemical characteristic with its host star, supporting a long-standing idea that also helps scientists investigate potentially habitable worlds. The breakthrough came from the first simultaneous measurement of gaseous magnesium and silicon in an exoplanet's atmosphere, using the Gemini South telescope, part of the International Gemini Observatory, which is partially funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and operated by NSF NOIRLab.
Located nearly 320 light-years away in the Libra constellation, WASP-189b belongs to an extreme category of planets called ultra-hot Jupiters (UHJ). These enormous worlds reach temperatures so intense that even materials normally found in solid rock can turn into gas. Elements such as magnesium (Mg), silicon (Si), and iron (Fe) can therefore be detected in their atmospheres. Astronomers identify these substances through spectroscopy, a method that separates light into different wavelengths to reveal the chemicals present.
An international research team led by Jorge Antonio Sanchez, a graduate student at Arizona State University (ASU), investigated WASP-189b with the high-resolution Immersion GRating INfrared Spectrograph (IGRINS). At the time, the instrument was installed on the Gemini South telescope in Chile.[1]
For the first time, researchers were able to measure magnesium and silicon together in the atmosphere of a planet beyond our Solar System. Their observations revealed that the proportion of magnesium to silicon on WASP-189b closely matches the ratio found in its parent star. This result provides the first direct observational support for a widely used assumption about the chemical relationship between stars and their planets, offering a valuable new way to investigate planetary origins and evolution.
"These discoveries show Gemini's ability to help us understand the characteristics of the remarkable zoo of exoplanets in our solar neighborhood," says Chris Davis, NSF Program Director for NOIRLab. "Such discoveries are only possible because of Gemini's cutting-edge instruments."
A Long-Suspected Connection Between Stars and Planets
Astronomers believe that giant planets such as WASP-189b formed within enormous disks of gas and dust surrounding young stars. These structures, called protoplanetary disks, provide the raw materials from which planets develop. The chemical makeup of a giant planet's outer atmosphere is thought to retain clues about the environment where it originally formed.
Because stars and their surrounding disks originate from the same cloud of material, scientists have long assumed that they contain similar proportions of rock-forming elements. In particular, the ratios of these elements in a disk are expected to resemble those measured in its central star.
This relationship has become an important tool for predicting the composition of rocky exoplanets. Until now, however, the assumption was supported primarily by evidence from our own Solar System. Astronomers had not directly measured the same relationship in a planet orbiting another star.
The discovery involving WASP-189b provides that missing observational evidence, strengthening the scientific basis for using stellar chemistry to understand the materials from which distant planets form.
"WASP-189b gives us a much-needed observational anchor in our understanding of terrestrial planet formation since it offers a measurable quantity that validates the presumed resemblance of stellar composition and the proportion of rocky material around host stars used to form planets," says Sanchez.
What Planetary Chemistry Could Reveal About Habitability
The implications reach beyond understanding how planets are assembled. This chemical relationship is also important in astrobiology, which investigates the possibility of life beyond Earth and the environmental conditions that could support it, including habitable environments within our Solar System.
By studying the elements present in a star, astronomers may be able to estimate the relative amounts of rock-forming materials available to its planets. These materials influence a planet's internal structure, geological activity, and chemical environment, all of which can affect whether conditions suitable for life might develop.
Earth provides a familiar example. The elements that make up our planet help determine processes such as plate tectonics, the generation of its protective magnetic field, and the movement of essential chemicals into the atmosphere, oceans, and soil. Together, these processes contribute to the environment that allows life to thrive.
As researchers work toward studying smaller, rocky exoplanets in greater detail, establishing a reliable connection between stellar chemistry and planetary composition becomes increasingly important. The WASP-189b findings provide a significant step in that direction.
Powerful Telescopes Open a New Window Into Alien Atmospheres
Obtaining these measurements requires instruments capable of distinguishing extremely fine details in the light collected from distant planetary atmospheres. According to the researchers, the necessary spectral resolution for this kind of analysis is currently available only through ground-based telescopes.
"Our study demonstrates the capability of ground-based, high-resolution spectrographs to constrain critical species like magnesium and silicon, which are two elemental building blocks from which rocky planets form," says study co-author Michael Line, Associate Professor at ASU. "This advancing capability opens an entirely new dimension in our study of exoplanet atmospheres."
The team expects future observations using multiple wavelengths and similarly precise instruments to uncover a wider range of elements in exoplanet atmospheres. Building a more complete picture of their chemical compositions could reveal additional clues about how planets form, how they change over time, and which conditions might favor habitability.
By connecting the chemistry of a distant planet to that of its star, astronomers now have new evidence supporting a principle that could help guide the search for potentially habitable worlds throughout the galaxy.
Notes
- IGRINS operated as a visiting instrument at Gemini South between 2022 and 2023 before returning to its home institution. Its successful performance led to the development of an updated version, IGRINS-2, which was subsequently commissioned as a permanent facility instrument for the Gemini North telescope in Hawai'i.

articles.title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
articles.text:
AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Indian Institute of Science (IISc)
- Summary:
- Scientists used artificial intelligence to uncover nearly 10,000 chemical reactions involved in transforming carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals, revealing crucial pathways that traditional models had missed. The discovery dramatically improved predictions of CO2 conversion and uncovered a surprising hydrogen reaction that could inspire more efficient catalysts.
- Share:
Scientists have uncovered thousands of previously overlooked chemical reactions that could help improve the conversion of carbon dioxide (CO2) into valuable fuels and industrial chemicals. By combining machine learning with advanced computer simulations, researchers at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) identified 9,389 individual reactions occurring on a copper catalyst, revealing unexpected chemical pathways that conventional models had missed.
The findings, published in Nature Communications, could help scientists develop more effective catalysts for transforming CO2 into useful products such as methanol. The research also uncovered a surprising way hydrogen can participate in these reactions, challenging established assumptions about how the process works.
One promising approach to recycling carbon dioxide is hydrogenation, which uses a catalyst to help CO2 react with hydrogen and form chemicals such as methanol. However, the process involves an enormous number of individual reactions taking place across the catalyst's surface. Simulating every possible step using quantum mechanics would require immense computing power, so researchers typically focus on a limited selection of reactions believed to be the most important. This simplification can leave hundreds of potentially critical reactions out of the picture.
"We began with a worry familiar to anyone who does mechanistic modeling: How do you know that your reaction network has not omitted the one step that matters?" says first author Anand Mohan Verma, who conducted the research as a CV Raman Postdoctoral Fellow at IISc and is now an Assistant Professor at the Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology Allahabad (MNNIT Allahabad).
AI Reveals Thousands of Overlooked Chemical Reactions
To overcome this limitation, the research team began by using quantum mechanics simulations to build a detailed database containing 152 chemical reactions. They then trained machine learning models to quickly estimate the energy barriers that additional reactions would need to overcome.
Using automated computational tools, the scientists examined the possible reactions involving 105 chemical species present on the catalyst surface. They also determined which transformations could take place in a single reaction step. This approach expanded their original network from just 152 reactions to 9,389.
The difference was significant. When the researchers relied on the smaller network, their model incorrectly identified formic acid as the main product rather than methanol. It also predicted substantially less CO2 conversion than experiments indicated.
"When we modeled the process using the 152 reactions considered initially, the network wrongly predicted formic acid, not methanol, as the major product, and underestimated how much CO2 gets converted. Only when we expanded the network to include thousands of additional, previously overlooked reactions did the predictions fall in line with what we and others see experimentally," explains corresponding author Ananth Govind Rajan, Associate Professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering, IISc.
Expanded Model Predicts 40 Times More CO2 Conversion
When the scientists incorporated the larger reaction network into a model of how quickly the chemical processes occur, the predicted amount of CO2 conversion increased by approximately 40 times compared with the original model.
The expanded model also correctly identified methanol and carbon monoxide as major products, bringing its predictions into agreement with experimental findings.
Experimental validation was carried out by G Valavarasu and Santhosh Kotni at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited's Green Research and Development Centre, along with Amol Amrute and colleagues at the Agency for Science, Technology, and Research in Singapore. Ambedkar Dukkipati, Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Automation at IISc, also contributed to the machine learning models.
A Surprising Hydrogen Pathway Challenges Conventional Chemistry
Beyond improving the predictions, the much larger reaction network exposed an unexpected mechanism involving hydrogen.
In several important reaction steps, hydrogen could be transferred to intermediate chemical compounds directly as molecular H2, rather than only through separate hydrogen atoms. Additional quantum mechanics calculations confirmed that this pathway can be especially favorable when hydrogen is transferred to intermediates containing oxygen.
This finding challenges a long-standing assumption about how hydrogen participates in catalytic reactions and could provide valuable clues for designing better catalysts.
"The idea that hydrogen can transfer as an intact molecule, without first splitting into atoms, runs against what most of us were taught," says co-author Shivam Chaturvedi, PhD student in the Department of Chemical Engineering, IISc. "This surfaced only because the network was large enough to allow for it, and the observation held up when we went back and computed those steps explicitly. This also suggests that catalysts that interact more strongly with H2 could potentially enhance pathways leading to methanol."
The researchers believe this unexpected mechanism could guide the development of catalysts that interact more effectively with molecular hydrogen, potentially improving the chemical pathways responsible for producing methanol from CO2.
The broader computational framework may also prove useful well beyond carbon dioxide hydrogenation. By integrating quantum mechanics simulations, machine learning, automated identification of chemical reactions, and models of reaction rates, the approach could help researchers investigate other important industrial processes.
Potential applications include CO2 reduction using different catalysts, nitrogen reduction, and water splitting. By revealing chemical steps that simpler models might miss, the technique offers scientists a more complete picture of complex catalytic reactions and new opportunities to improve processes used to produce fuels and chemicals.

Journal Reference:

Data-driven massive reaction networks reveal mechanistic pathways underlying catalytic CO2 hydrogenation. Nature Communications, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-77080-4

articles.title: Is the brain actually 2 nervous systems smooshed together? A new study claims it is.
articles.text:
Is the brain actually 2 nervous systems smooshed together? A new study claims it is.
A recent study may reshape our understanding of brain evolution and open new avenues for studying neurological diseases.
Recent research challenges a long-standing idea about how the brain develops: Rather than arising from a single source, the brain may emerge from two distinct populations of cells, the study finds.
"The brain appears as one organ," said study co-author Kyle Loh, an associate professor of developmental biology at Stanford University. "However, we discovered that the front part of the brain and the back part of the brain come from different sources, which are pushed together to create the appearance of a single organ," Loh told Live Science in an email.
The findings, published in September in the journal Nature Neuroscience, not only challenge established models of how the brain forms but may also explain why researchers have struggled to grow certain types of brain cells in the laboratory. The scientists say the work could offer new ways to investigate diseases that affect the brainstem, the "stalk" that connects the brain to the spinal cord.
Two developmental journeys
The human brain is divided into three main regions — called the forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain — that perform different but interconnected functions.
The forebrain, which includes the cerebral hemispheres, is involved in higher-level cognitive processes, such as language, planning and abstract thinking. The midbrain, the uppermost part of the brainstem, connects the forebrain and the hindbrain and acts as a key relay center for sensory information and movement control. The hindbrain — which includes the bottom of the brainstem, along with other structures — also helps to coordinate movement, as well as regulate essential functions such as breathing, sleep and heart rate.
Historically, the hindbrain has been difficult to study. One reason is that scientists have faced persistent challenges in generating functional hindbrain neurons in laboratory conditions.
To help understand why, Loh and his team looked at the early stages of embryonic development in lab mice. They focused on gastrulation, the point when cells begin to organize into structures that will later form different organs. The researchers identified two distinct populations of immature cells that would go on to give rise to nervous system tissue, including the brain.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
One cell population expressed a gene called Otx2, which helps to direct the early development of the forebrain and midbrain. The second group of cells expressed the gene Gbx2, which is involved in the development of the midbrain and hindbrain.
The functions of these genes were already known, but their distinct expression in these two groups of cells was revealed by the new research. The cell populations remained distinct as they developed into full-fledged nervous tissue, rather than overlapping.
The team also examined chromatin, the molecular structure that packages DNA tightly inside the nucleus and helps regulate which genes a cell can use. The two cell populations show different chromatin configurations, the team found, which further supports the idea that they follow separate developmental pathways.
That may help to explain why scientists' attempts to grow hindbrain neurons have been largely unsuccessful.
"Previous attempts to make hindbrain neurons likely tried to coax forebrain and midbrain progenitors into hindbrain cells, which our study shows is not possible," study co-author Rayyan Jokhai, a graduate student in Loh's lab, said in a statement.
Why it matters
Using the information uncovered in their experiments, the researchers successfully guided human stem cells to transform into functional hindbrain motor neurons, which are involved in controlling movement. Specifically, these cells produced proteins characteristic of the hard-to-grow hindbrain regions that help control muscles of the face and those involved in swallowing.
In several neurological diseases, including spinal muscular atrophy and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, motor neurons deteriorate and affected patients can lose their ability to swallow, speak and breathe independently.
"We cannot sample living motor neurons from a patient's hindbrain to watch how these diseases attack these neurons," Loh said. "Growing these hindbrain motor neurons in a dish gives us a way to investigate these diseases." Looking forward, the team aims to use their findings to study these diseases and pinpoint new treatments.
The new findings could also reveal something fundamental about the evolution of vertebrate animals.
The study authors investigated whether the two developmental pathways were unique to humans or reflected a much older evolutionary arrangement. They turned to previously published data on other species — including macaques (Macaca), zebrafish (Danio rerio) and chickens (Gallus gallus domesticus) — and again found two distinct cell populations expressing the two key genes.
And even in acorn worms — a marine invertebrate whose evolution diverged from vertebrates about 550 million years ago — they again found these two distinct groups of cells.
Related stories
"The Stanford discovery establishes that the deep ancestry of the vertebrate brain is fundamentally modular," said Anna Di Cosmo, a professor of biology at the University of Naples Federico II in Italy who wasn't involved with the study. "The developmental separation between the anterior lineage (forebrain/midbrain) and the posterior lineage (hindbrain) is traceably ancient," Cosmo told Live Science in an email.
Loh's team speculates that these developmental trajectories seen in the womb may suggest that the two cell populations once belonged to two separate nervous systems. "Later in evolution, these two nervous systems may have been pushed together to give rise to the appearance of one integrated brain," Loh said.
However, the study doesn't reveal exactly when the two pathways arose or establish how they integrated. "It is important to emphasize that this is only an idea, and it might change as scientists learn more," Loh said.

A., Greenfeld, H., Wong, A., Qu, Y., Petkovic, A. S., Miao, Y., Garcia, K. C., . . . Loh, K. M. (2026). Two parallel neural ectoderm progenitors contribute to the developing brain.
